standard.title: Character form and function, complex grammatical structures
standard.description: apply knowledge of character form and function, and complex grammatical structures and features, to predict meaning and to compose a wide range of texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply morphological knowledge and use the full sentence-type range in composed texts (AC9LCH8U02). They have used modal, tense-expression and exclamatory structures. They have not yet used print dictionaries for character lookup, explored polysemy across complex contexts, applied auxiliary verbs, used advanced punctuation conventions, or compared simplified and traditional character forms.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply knowledge of character form and function and complex grammatical structures and features to predict meaning and compose a wide range of texts — including using print resources, polysemy analysis, complex modality, and advanced punctuation.

nodes.label: Advanced character analysis and print resource use
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use knowledge of character components to look up new characters in print dictionaries, predict meanings of complex characters using pictographic knowledge, and explore polysemy in context.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a print dictionary to look up at least three unfamiliar characters using component knowledge, and identify at least two examples of polysemous characters used differently in different contexts.
nodes.typical_width: Use component knowledge to look up characters in print dictionaries; predict meanings of complex characters using pictographic knowledge; determine precise meanings of morphemes by context; explore polysemous characters across different contexts; compare simplified and traditional character forms.
wider: Research the relationship between simplified and traditional character forms for a set of characters — explain what was simplified, why, and what (if anything) is lost or gained
Investigate a polysemous character — identify all its documented meanings, explain the semantic relationship between them, and create examples showing each meaning in context
nodes.hinge_reason: Advanced character analysis and print dictionary use are the productive literacy prerequisites for independent wide reading and composition at Y9-10. Students who cannot use print resources or analyse character polysemy are dependent on digital tools and cannot develop the independent literacy the descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Print dictionary use and polysemy analysis require systematic application of component and morphological knowledge — students need a framework for navigating print dictionaries and for determining which meaning of a polysemous character is active in context. Explicit strategy instruction followed by independent practice builds this capacity.

success_criteria: Looks up at least three characters in a print dictionary using component knowledge
Identifies at least two polysemous characters and explains the different meaning in each context

nodes.label: Complex modality and advanced grammatical features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply knowledge of modal and auxiliary verbs, complex tense expression, and advanced punctuation conventions across a range of text types.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a text demonstrating correct use of at least three different complex grammatical features — modal verbs, auxiliary verbs, or advanced punctuation — with appropriate accuracy for the text type.
nodes.typical_width: Apply modal verbs and auxiliary verbs in a range of text types; apply knowledge of tense in formal and informal contexts; use advanced punctuation including quotation marks for sarcasm, brackets, ellipsis; respond appropriately to sarcasm, exclamatory sentences and factual statements; identify how sentence structures convey messages effectively.
wider: Analyse how modal and auxiliary verbs create different degrees of certainty, obligation or possibility — create a set of examples showing the full range and explain the distinctions
Investigate advanced punctuation conventions in the target language that have no direct English equivalent — explain the function of each and create examples demonstrating correct use

response_modes.reason: Complex modality and advanced grammatical features require repeated production across varied text types before they become reliable. Targeted writing tasks across different genres — formal report, personal narrative, persuasive text — build the flexible grammatical competence the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Advanced grammatical analysis at this level — particularly the comparison of simplified/traditional forms and the systematic analysis of polysemy and modality — develops a depth of metalinguistic understanding that has transferable academic value. Width investment here builds genuine linguistic scholarship.
success_criteria: Produces a text demonstrating correct use of at least three different complex grammatical features
Applies advanced punctuation conventions correctly in at least one text

nodes.label: Composing a wide range of texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply full character and grammatical knowledge to compose and respond to a wide range of texts — including formal, informal, literary and multimodal — across diverse contexts and purposes.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose at least two texts of different types (e.g. a formal report and a narrative) demonstrating full writing system knowledge and appropriate grammar for each text type.
nodes.typical_width: Apply full character and grammatical knowledge across a wide range of text types — reports, plans, diaries, literary texts, multimodal productions; adapt grammar and vocabulary for context, purpose and audience; respond to diverse stimuli demonstrating appropriate grammatical choices.
wider: Compose a text that deliberately uses a specific grammatical feature for rhetorical effect — explain the choice and compare the effect with an alternative grammatical approach
Review and annotate own extended writing for grammatical accuracy and appropriateness — identify patterns of error or inconsistency and develop a targeted improvement plan

response_modes.reason: Wide-range text composition integrates advanced character analysis (node 1) and complex grammatical features (node 2) into the full productive literacy demand of Y9-10. The teaching investment is in creating varied, genuine composition tasks across text types — not only narrative or only formal — that require students to deploy their full grammatical and textual knowledge.

success_criteria: Composes at least two texts of different types demonstrating full writing system knowledge
Grammar and vocabulary choices are appropriate for each text type and purpose
